It seems that Geth and Besu use a number as an input (so far on my checks..), so the spec might need updated I was just trying to test on Erigon, but the API has not been implemented yet. So I haven't been able to verify yet. Here is my impression. I would like to know what happens with the "earliest" parameter too: `feeHistory` Which enables a query to get the BaseFee Which has three parameters: - `blockCount` - **Required** - *How many blocks of fee history are wanted?* - "Number of blocks in the requested range. Between 1 and 1024 blocks can be requested in a single query. Less than requested may be returned if not all blocks are available." - Formatted as a hexadecimal representation of the integer as a string. - e.g. for 25 blocks, `str(hex(25)) = "0x19"`. - `newestBlock` - **Required** - *What is the most recent block that is wanted?* - "Highest number block of the requested range." - Formatted as either of: - A hexadecimal representation of the integer as a string. - e.g. for block 5093543, `str(hex(5093543)) = "0x4db8a7"`. - *This is the most recent block that is wanted*. - A descriptor string, one of: - "earliest". - *Unclear TODO.* - "latest". - *The block that was just mined.* - "pending". - *The block that is about to be mined.* - `rewardPercentiles` - **Optional** - *Which percentiles of the gas premium are wanted?* - "A monotonically increasing list of percentile values to sample from each block's effective priority fees per gas in ascending order, weighted by gas used." - E.g. 0th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles. - Formatted as floating point values between 0 and 100 as a string. - E.g. For the example above: - ["0", "25", "50", "75", "100"] - Or percentiles 0-3rd with 0.5 increments, and the 80th percentile: - ["0", "0.5", "1", "1.5", "2", "2.5", "3", "80"] So I was interpreting it, as you say, as hex in a string format Copied from the spec: ``` { "name": "blockCount", "description": "Number of blocks in the requested range. Between 1 and 1024 blocks can be requested in a single query. Less than requested may be returned if not all blocks are available.", "required": true, "schema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Integer" } } ``` I was using this as a guide: https://playground.open-rpc.org/?uiSchema%5BappBar%5D%5Bui:splitView%5D=false&schemaUrl=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/master/json-rpc/spec.json&uiSchema%5BappBar%5D%5Bui:input%5D=false (Feedback welcome on any of the above interpretations) <@!743395542196944977> thank you!, yes hence the question, either the spec is incorrect, or is a small mistake on the rpc calls > I would like to know what happens with the "earliest" parameter <@!743395542196944977> is there a reason it wouldn't behave as usual, grabbing the genesis block? <@!680337202521440470> checking the besu output is not returning hex either I really wasn't sure. So genesis it is! Thanks Would it make sense to double the default gas limit in Hardhat Network when using EIP-1559? Or maybe this is a better question: by reading the EIP I don't see any new flexibility wrt the block gas limit. Is it because the extra flexibility in the target, not in the limit? Does this mean that the block gas limit should be raised to avoid an effective decrease in total gas used per block? <@!453707755765760021> I'm not super familiar with hardhard, but any network with 1559 enabled should double its pre-1559 gas limit if it wants to maintain the same average throughput it's worth noting that 1559 works best for networks with a constant stream of txns, if your network has bursts of usage and testnet ETH, then you may actually be fine keeping the previous gas limit as most of the time your blocks will be empty and you can just pay a higher base fee during your bursts of usage thanks, this confirms what I had in mind This is also a good point. excerpts.author: perama
excerpts.content:
`feeHistory`

Which enables a query to get the BaseFee Which has three parameters:

- `blockCount`
    - **Required**
    - *How many blocks of fee history are wanted?*
    - "Number of blocks in the requested range. Between 1 and 1024 blocks can be requested in a
    single query. Less than requested may be returned if not all blocks are available."
    - Formatted as a hexadecimal representation of the integer as a string.
        - e.g. for 25 blocks, `str(hex(25)) = "0x19"`.
- `newestBlock`
    - **Required**
    - *What is the most recent block that is wanted?*
    - "Highest number block of the requested range."
    - Formatted as either of:
        - A hexadecimal representation of the integer as a string.
            - e.g. for block 5093543, `str(hex(5093543)) = "0x4db8a7"`.
            - *This is the most recent block that is wanted*.
        - A descriptor string, one of:
            - "earliest".
                - *Unclear TODO.*
            - "latest".
                - *The block that was just mined.*
            - "pending".
                - *The block that is about to be mined.*
- `rewardPercentiles`
    - **Optional**
    - *Which percentiles of the gas premium are wanted?*
    - "A monotonically increasing list of percentile values to sample from each block's
    effective priority fees per gas in ascending order, weighted by gas used."
    - E.g. 0th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles.
    - Formatted as floating point values between 0 and 100 as a string.
        - E.g. For the example above:
            - ["0", "25", "50", "75", "100"]
        - Or percentiles 0-3rd with 0.5 increments, and the 80th percentile:
            - ["0", "0.5", "1", "1.5", "2", "2.5", "3", "80"]

excerpts.author: perama
excerpts.content: So I was interpreting it, as you say, as hex in a string format

Copied from the spec:

```
                not all blocks are available.",
            "required": true,
            "schema": {

            }
        }
```

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content:
Would it make sense to double the default gas limit in Hardhat Network when using EIP-1559? 

Or maybe this is a better question: by reading the EIP I don't see any new flexibility wrt the block gas limit. Is it because the extra flexibility in the target, not in the limit? Does this mean that the block gas limit should be raised to avoid an effective decrease in total gas used per block?

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: <@!453707755765760021> I'm not super familiar with hardhard, but any network with 1559 enabled should double its pre-1559 gas limit if it wants to maintain the same average throughput

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: it's worth noting that 1559 works best for networks with a constant stream of txns, if your network has bursts of usage and testnet ETH, then you may actually be fine keeping the previous gas limit as most of the time your blocks will be empty and you can just pay a higher base fee during your bursts of usage

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content: thanks, this confirms what I had in mind

excerpts.author: patricio.palladino
excerpts.content: This is also a good point. We mine a block per tx normally, and I suspect most of the time the base fee will drop to the minimum, so we are adding a custom RPC method to let users choose the base fee of the next block.
